_comment: Raptor's egg library (library/README.md). Based on the TeamSpeak 6 eggs in pterodactyl/application-eggs (MIT).
name: TeamSpeak 6
author: support@raptorpanel.net
description: TeamSpeak 6 is the newest TeamSpeak voice server, for low-latency voice chat with channels and permissions. The egg runs it on the server's port with its own SQLite database.

installation.script:
#!/bin/bash
# TeamSpeak 6: downloads the TeamSpeak 6 server from TeamSpeak's GitHub
# releases for this CPU and checks it against GitHub's checksum. The
# database, uploaded files, keys and logs are never touched: only the
# server's own files from the release are replaced.
set -euo pipefail
cd /mnt/server

repo=teamspeak/teamspeak6-server
fail() { echo "$1"; exit 1; }
# GitHub releases, through the installer's gh-release (GitHub's API has a
# low anonymous limit). gh_tag <latest|tag> prints the release's tag;
# returns 1 when there's no such release, 2 when GitHub can't be reached.
gh_tag() {
    local out
    out=$(gh-release tag "$repo" "$1" 2>&1) && { echo "$out"; return 0; }
    case "$out" in *"has no release"* | *"no releases"*) return 1 ;; *) return 2 ;; esac
}
offline="GitHub can't be reached right now, or is limiting downloads. Reinstall to try again in a few minutes."
case "$(uname -m)" in
    x86_64) arch='(amd64|x86_64)' ;;
    aarch64) arch='(arm64|aarch64)' ;;
    *) fail "TeamSpeak 6 has no build for this CPU ($(uname -m))." ;;
esac

version="${TS_VERSION:-latest}"
case "$version" in latest|v*) ;; *) version="v$version" ;; esac
rc=0; tag=$(gh_tag "$version") || rc=$?
if [ "$rc" = 1 ]; then
    latest=$(gh_tag latest) || fail "$offline"
    fail "TeamSpeak 6 has no version ${TS_VERSION}. Set Version to latest, or to a release such as $latest."
fi
[ "$rc" = 0 ] || fail "$offline"
version=$tag
assets=$(gh-release assets "$repo" "$version") || fail "$offline"
read -r asset sum < <(grep -E "linux[-_]$arch.*\.tar\.(xz|bz2|gz) " <<<"$assets" | head -n 1) || true
[ -n "${asset:-}" ] || fail "TeamSpeak $version has no Linux server for this CPU. Choose another version."

if [ "$sum" != - ] && [ -x tsserver ] && [ "$(cat .raptor-teamspeak 2>/dev/null)" = "$sum" ]; then
    echo "TeamSpeak $version is already installed."
else
    echo "Downloading TeamSpeak $version"
    tmp=/mnt/server/.raptor-build
    rm -rf "$tmp" && mkdir -p "$tmp"
    trap 'rm -rf "$tmp"' EXIT
    gh-release download "$repo" "$version" "$asset" "$tmp/server.tar" || fail "The download failed or didn't match GitHub's checksum. Reinstall to try again."
    mkdir "$tmp/x"
    tar -xf "$tmp/server.tar" -C "$tmp/x"
    src="$tmp/x"
    # Some releases have everything in one folder.
    if [ ! -e "$src/tsserver" ] && [ "$(ls -A "$src" | wc -l)" = 1 ]; then src="$src/$(ls -A "$src")"; fi
    [ -f "$src/tsserver" ] || fail "The download has no tsserver in it. Choose another version."
    cp -a "$src/." .
    rm -rf "$tmp"
    chmod +x tsserver
    echo "$sum" > .raptor-teamspeak
fi
echo "Installed TeamSpeak $version. On the first start, the console shows the privilege key that makes you server admin."

variables.name: Version
variables.description: The TeamSpeak 6 server version to install, such as v6.0.0-beta13.1, or latest.

variables.name: License
variables.description: Set to accept, this accepts TeamSpeak's server license (LICENSE in the server's folder). Empty, the server asks on the console.

variables.name: Query admin password
variables.description: Sets the password of the serveradmin query account. Empty keeps the one the server made on its first start.

variables.name: File transfer port
variables.description: The port file transfers (uploads, avatars, icons) listens on. Add it to the server's ports first.

variables.name: SSH query
variables.description: Set it to 1 to turn on the SSH query interface.

variables.name: SSH query port
variables.description: The port the SSH query interface listens on. Add it to the server's ports first.

variables.name: HTTP query
variables.description: Set it to 1 to turn on the HTTP query interface.

variables.name: HTTP query port
variables.description: The port the HTTP query interface listens on. Add it to the server's ports first.

variables.name: HTTPS query
variables.description: Set it to 1 to turn on the HTTPS query interface, with the certificate and key below.

variables.name: HTTPS query port
variables.description: The port the HTTPS query interface listens on. Add it to the server's ports first.

variables.name: HTTPS certificate
variables.description: The certificate file for the HTTPS query interface, uploaded to the server's folder, such as cert.pem.

variables.name: HTTPS private key
variables.description: The private key file for the certificate, uploaded to the server's folder, such as key.pem.

variables.name: S3 file transfer
variables.description: Set it to 1 to turn on storing file transfers in S3 storage instead of the server's folder.

variables.name: S3 access key
variables.description: The access key for the S3 storage.

variables.name: S3 secret key
variables.description: The secret key for the S3 storage.

variables.name: S3 bucket
variables.description: The S3 bucket file transfers are stored in.

variables.name: S3 domain
variables.description: The S3 storage's endpoint, such as s3.example.com.

variables.name: S3 region
variables.description: The S3 storage's region, such as eu-central-1.
